sprint_note: Adds FSRS as a second, persistently 50/50-assigned scheduling algorithm alongside Classic (wrapping, never editing, the existing compute_next_due_at), a new fsrs_card_state table, a new append-only review_events table, additive scheduler/assignment columns on flashcard_review_state plus a one-time guarded migration backfill, a scheduler badge on the review card, and a first-version GET /experiment/summary comparison dashboard — the existing due-queue selection/ordering mechanism is completely untouched. NOTE (R-OPS-BP-01): 00_architecture/architecture.json and scaffolding.json (the repo's seed baseline) predate Sprints 03/06/07/08/09 (images, exploration, examinations, roadmap, question levels, nuggets) — same staleness Sprint09_Nuggets/10_scaffolding.json already documented and deviated from. This sprint's artifacts are therefore NOT copied from that stale seed; they describe this sprint's changes directly against the current live code (read in full for this design pass), listing only touched/new files rather than re-diffing a 5-sprints-out-of-date baseline.
summary: Introduces FSRS as a second scheduling algorithm, persistently A/B-assigned 50/50 against the existing Classic scheduler per flashcard, with both algorithms writing next_due_at/review_interval through the existing single interface so the card-selection mechanism is completely untouched, plus a scheduler badge and a first-version experiment comparison dashboard.

classification.why_application: Which spaced-repetition algorithm a card uses, how it is assigned, and how its outcomes are compared are EssayCards-specific domain decisions about this app's own learning model — not a reusable technical capability. The Classic formula and the FSRS wrapper both exist only to answer 'what should this app's next_due_at be', which has meaning solely inside EssayCards' existing due-queue/session semantics documented in CLAUDE.md.
non_goals: Switching individual cards between algorithms after assignment
Redesigned review selection, ordering, resurfacing, or Focus/Review eligibility
FSRS-native learning/established vocabulary anywhere in code, UI, or docs
Major changes to the flashcard UI beyond the badge and dashboard
Advanced statistical analysis or automatic winner selection on the dashboard
A retroactive FSRS state reconstruction for cards with real review history (no per-review history table exists to replay — see contracts.invariants)
An admin escape hatch to reassign an FSRS-cohort card back to Classic (rollback = kill switch stops new assignment only, per Phase B §7)
classification.not_platform: FSRS is being integrated as a second scheduling engine feeding EssayCards' own next_due_at/review_interval model, not exposed as a reusable spaced-repetition service for other Atlas applications. The assignment mechanism, its persisted metadata, and the dashboard are meaningful only in terms of EssayCards' own due-queue vocabulary (new/learning/established, RECENT/BACKLOG, Focus/Review). If another Atlas app later needs its own scheduling comparison, that is a platform-extraction question to consider then, not now.

POST /api/essaycards/flashcards/{flashcard_id}/review — unchanged request/response contract; internally dispatches to ClassicScheduler or FSRSScheduler per the card's persisted scheduler and additionally persists fsrs_card_state (fsrs cards only) and one review_events row (every review) in the same transaction
GET /api/essaycards/experiment/summary — new Dataset endpoint, always exactly two rows ('classic', 'fsrs'), the experiment comparison dashboard's data source

New-card creation (backend/ingest.py essay/section ingest, POST /flashcards/upsert, POST /flashcards/exploration/import's create_card action) — each of the three existing was_inserted-gated INSERT sites additionally performs a one-time, permanent scheduler assignment; no change to any of their request/response shapes
invariants: backend/scheduling.py::compute_next_due_at and VALID_GRADES are byte-for-byte unchanged by this sprint. All existing unit tests in tests/test_scheduling.py must keep passing unmodified.

Both ClassicScheduler.review(...) and FSRSScheduler.review(...) write exactly next_due_at, review_interval, and last_reviewed_at through the existing flashcard_review_state columns and the existing single UPDATE statement shape in review_flashcard — FSRS's own stability/difficulty/state are a SEPARATE, additional persisted concept (essaycards.fsrs_card_state) and are never confused with or substituted for review_interval. FSRS calculates next_due_at; EssayCards persists it through the existing field, exactly as Classic already does.

The existing 24-hour learning/established threshold (review_interval >= interval '24 hours'), the RECENT/BACKLOG due-queue categorization and ordering (GET /flashcards/due), the seven forecast bands (GET /flashcards/stats), and Focus/Review eligibility are read ONLY from next_due_at/last_reviewed_at/review_interval — none of these queries reads or branches on the scheduler column. This sprint adds zero WHERE/ORDER BY changes to list_due_flashcards or flashcard_queue_stats beyond the new scheduler column appearing as an additive SELECT field (same precedent as nugget_id, Sprint09).

FSRS short learning/relearning intervals (sub-hour, a real default-configuration output of py-fsrs per Agent 3's research) are accepted as-is and flow through next_due_at exactly like Classic's own 5s/1min/20min floors already do — resurfaced via the existing RECENT category mechanism. No separate FSRS queue, no scheduler-type-specific selection branch anywhere.

fsrs.Scheduler is constructed once, module-level, as Scheduler(desired_retention=0.9) with library-default 21-parameter weights (FSRS-6) and library-default learning_steps/relearning_steps (NOT overridden to learning_steps=()). No FSRS optimizer use this sprint.
Rating mapping is a direct 1:1 name match: grade strings 'again'/'hard'/'good'/'easy' map to fsrs.Rating.Again/Hard/Good/Easy by name, via one fixed dict — no numeric or semantic translation.

Every datetime passed into py-fsrs (review_card's review_datetime, and any datetime read back off a loaded Card) is normalized to exactly `.astimezone(timezone.utc)` before use — py-fsrs raises ValueError on a naive datetime and raises on a tz-aware-but-not-identically-timezone.utc datetime (R-CON-AL-06: the single time authority remains the same Postgres `select now()` read already used by review_flashcard; this is a representation conversion of that same value, not a second time source).

essaycards.fsrs_card_state.raw_state (the full fsrs.Card.to_dict() output) is the SOLE source of truth for reconstructing a Card object (Card.from_dict(raw_state)) on the next review. The discrete columns (stability, difficulty, fsrs_state, step, last_review_at) exist only for dashboard queryability/audit and must always be written from the SAME to_dict() call that produced raw_state in the same statement — never derived independently, never allowed to drift from raw_state.

A brand-new FSRS-cohort card being reviewed for the first time (no existing essaycards.fsrs_card_state row) starts from a fresh fsrs.Card() (library defaults: State.Learning, step=0, stability=None, difficulty=None) — the library's own internal card_id (an auto-generated int, unrelated to the flashcard's uuid) is never persisted or round-tripped anywhere in EssayCards' schema; it exists only inside raw_state for the library's own bookkeeping and is never read back out by EssayCards code.

review_flashcard writes flashcard_review_state (last_reviewed_at/next_due_at/review_interval/updated_at), fsrs_card_state (fsrs cards only, upsert), and one essaycards.review_events row (every review, both schedulers) inside the SAME transaction as the existing single commit() call — a review can never persist its new due date while failing to persist its scheduler state or its review-event record (mission §5 'a review cannot save its due date while failing to save its associated scheduler state or review history').

review_events.was_due is computed as (the card's next_due_at BEFORE this review) <= (the single now() read for this review) — a technical/diagnostic record of whether the due-queue's own base eligibility condition held for this review (mirroring GET /flashcards/due's unchanged `next_due_at <= now()`). Because that base condition applies to every session type and a card only ever re-enters the queue once its own next_due_at has elapsed, was_due evaluates true for virtually every review the application can produce — including RECENT-category rapid retries — so it cannot by itself separate ordinary due-review evidence from immediate-relearning/rapid-retry reviews, and the experiment dashboard does NOT use it for that purpose. The dashboard instead restricts ordinary_due_reviews/recall_rate/failures to review_events rows where prior_review_interval >= interval '24 hours' — i.e. the card had already graduated to established BEFORE this review, mirroring the app's existing 24-hour learning/established threshold (CLAUDE.md). A rapid retry always follows a short (learning-phase) prior_review_interval and is excluded by that filter regardless of was_due (mission §7: do not count multiple rapid retries as independent evidence of long-term retention). was_due remains stored as an audit/diagnostic field only.

Scheduler assignment happens exactly once per flashcard, at creation, inside the existing `if was_inserted:` gate already present at all three insertion call sites (backend/ingest.py::_upsert_flashcard, backend/routers/flashcards.py::_upsert_question, backend/exploration.py::execute_plan's create_card branch) — never on update/re-ingest/regeneration, inheriting the same idempotency already proven for review-state seeding at those exact gates (Agent 4's finding). No endpoint request body anywhere accepts a scheduler field; assignment is exclusively a server-side side effect of card creation and the one-time migration backfill below. There is no admin or API path to reassign an already-assigned card.

Assignment is decided by backend/scheduling.py::decide_scheduler_assignment(flashcard_id, migrated_never_reviewed=False) -> (scheduler, reason): if the kill switch (ESSAYCARDS_FSRS_EXPERIMENT_ENABLED, default true, read fresh from os.environ on every call — never cached at import — so tests can monkeypatch it) is false, returns ('classic', 'assignment_disabled_classic') unconditionally; otherwise returns a scheduler chosen by a stable hash of flashcard_id mod 2 (sha256(str(flashcard_id)) mod 2 — no stored RNG seed, naturally balanced ~50/50 in expectation across any stratum without a stratified sampler, computed once and persisted, never recomputed), with reason 'new_card_random' if migrated_never_reviewed is False else 'migrated_never_reviewed_random'.

scheduler_assignment_reason is a closed, fixed vocabulary of exactly four values, enforced by a CHECK constraint: 'new_card_random' (a genuinely new card, or the kill switch was disabled), 'assignment_disabled_classic' (kill switch was disabled at creation time), 'migrated_never_reviewed_random' (a pre-existing but never-reviewed card, assigned at the one-time migration backfill using the same balanced mechanism as a new card), 'legacy_retained_classic' (a pre-existing card with real review history — see the migration invariant below).

Migration (10_schema.sql, folded into schema.sql, run idempotently at every startup via init_schema()) is a one-time, additive, sentinel-guarded backfill, gated on scheduler_assigned_at IS NULL so a rerun is a no-op: (1) every flashcard_review_state row with last_reviewed_at IS NOT NULL (already reviewed under Classic pre-sprint) is set to scheduler='classic', scheduler_assignment_reason='legacy_retained_classic' — no FSRS state is ever created for such a card, and next_due_at/review_interval/last_reviewed_at are NEVER touched by this backfill (per Phase B §5: py-fsrs's only history-based initialization path, reschedule_card, requires a complete ordered per-review rating history EssayCards has never persisted, so reliable FSRS initialization is impossible for any card with real history — the mission's documented fallback applies to every such card, not a subset); (2) every row with last_reviewed_at IS NULL (existing but never reviewed) is assigned via the identical balanced mechanism as a brand-new card, because a fresh fsrs.Card() IS the correct FSRS initialization for a never-reviewed card — zero replay needed.

Both migration UPDATEs use Postgres-native hashing (hashtext(flashcard_id::text) % 2) rather than the Python sha256-based helper used for new-card assignment at INSERT time — this is a deliberate, safe divergence: the two cohorts (existing never-reviewed cards at migration time vs. cards created from this sprint forward) are disjoint and never need cross-language hash parity with each other.

All read endpoints returning UI-visible tabular data continue to return Dataset per R-CON-BP-04: GET /flashcards/due (extended) and the new GET /experiment/summary. No FSRS-native vocabulary (stability, difficulty, FSRS state names) appears in any ColumnSchema label, UI string, or the scheduler badge — the badge shows exactly 'Classic' or 'FSRS' (plain algorithm names) per CLAUDE.md's glossary discipline and 00_draft.md §6.
failure_modes: NOT_FOUND — POST /flashcards/{id}/review with an unknown flashcard_id — 404 ApiError (unchanged from pre-sprint behavior)
VALIDATION_ERROR — POST /flashcards/{id}/review with a malformed/invalid grade — 400 ApiError (unchanged from pre-sprint behavior; scheduler dispatch happens only after grade validation succeeds)

Startup/migration failure — if the additive schema.sql (including the two guarded backfill UPDATEs) fails to apply, init_schema() raises and the existing main.py startup retry loop (10 attempts, 3s apart) applies unchanged; the app never serves traffic against a partially-migrated schema because schema.sql runs as one transaction

FSRS library invariant violation (documented as a risk, not a normal API failure mode — it can only occur from a corrupted or hand-edited raw_state row, never from normal application flow): fsrs.Card.from_dict raising on a malformed persisted raw_state would surface as an unhandled 500 from review_flashcard; there is no user input path that can trigger this, since raw_state is only ever written by FSRSScheduler.review itself

internal_flow.name: scheduler_review_dispatch
internal_flow.description: review_flashcard (backend/routers/flashcards.py) reads scheduler (in addition to the existing last_reviewed_at) from the card's flashcard_review_state row, reads existing fsrs_card_state.raw_state for that card when scheduler=='fsrs' (may be None), then calls (ClassicScheduler() if scheduler=='classic' else FSRSScheduler()).review(grade, last_reviewed_at, now, existing_state) -> SchedulerResult(next_due_at, review_interval, extra_state).

internal_flow.name: classic_scheduler_review
internal_flow.description: ClassicScheduler.review(...) is a thin pass-through: calls the UNCHANGED compute_next_due_at(grade, last_reviewed_at, now), returns SchedulerResult(next_due_at, next_due_at - now, extra_state=None). Ignores existing_state entirely (Classic never persists extra per-card state beyond the existing three columns).

internal_flow.name: fsrs_scheduler_review
internal_flow.description: FSRSScheduler.review(...): now_utc = now.astimezone(timezone.utc); card = Card.from_dict(existing_state['raw_state']) if existing_state else Card() (fresh Learning-state card for a card's first-ever FSRS review); rating = the fixed grade->Rating dict lookup; new_card, _log = the module-level Scheduler(desired_retention=0.9).review_card(card, rating, review_datetime=now_utc); returns SchedulerResult(next_due_at=new_card.due, review_interval=new_card.due - now_utc, extra_state={stability, difficulty, fsrs_state: int(new_card.state), step, last_review_at: new_card.last_review, raw_state: new_card.to_dict()}).

internal_flow.name: review_transactional_writes
internal_flow.description: Inside the existing single transaction (same get_db()/commit() block already in review_flashcard): (a) UPDATE flashcard_review_state SET last_reviewed_at=now, next_due_at=result.next_due_at, review_interval=result.review_interval, updated_at=now — same statement shape as pre-sprint, values now sourced from the SchedulerResult instead of a direct compute_next_due_at call; (b) if scheduler=='fsrs': INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (flashcard_id) DO UPDATE into fsrs_card_state from result.extra_state; (c) always: INSERT one row into review_events (flashcard_id, scheduler, grade, reviewed_at=now, was_due = (pre-review next_due_at <= now), prior_review_interval = the row's review_interval value BEFORE this update, resulting_review_interval = result.review_interval). All three writes commit together.
inputs: the pre-review flashcard_review_state row (next_due_at, review_interval) read in step 1

internal_flow.name: scheduler_assignment_decision
internal_flow.description: backend/scheduling.py::decide_scheduler_assignment(flashcard_id, migrated_never_reviewed=False) -> (scheduler, reason). Reads ESSAYCARDS_FSRS_EXPERIMENT_ENABLED from os.environ fresh on every call (default true); if disabled, returns ('classic', 'assignment_disabled_classic'). Otherwise computes sha256(str(flashcard_id).encode()).digest()[0] % 2 (or equivalent stable hash) to pick 'classic' or 'fsrs', with reason 'new_card_random' (migrated_never_reviewed False) or 'migrated_never_reviewed_random' (True).

internal_flow.name: new_card_seeding_ingest
internal_flow.description: backend/ingest.py::_upsert_flashcard, inside its existing `if row['was_inserted']:` block, calls decide_scheduler_assignment(row['id']) and extends the existing flashcard_review_state INSERT to also set scheduler, scheduler_assigned_at=now(), scheduler_assignment_reason, experiment_version='sprint10_v1'.
outputs: flashcard_review_state row seeded with scheduler metadata, exactly as today for last_reviewed_at/next_due_at/review_interval

internal_flow.name: new_card_seeding_upsert
internal_flow.description: backend/routers/flashcards.py::_upsert_question, inside its existing `if row['was_inserted']:` block, applies the identical treatment as step 6.
outputs: flashcard_review_state row seeded with scheduler metadata

internal_flow.name: new_card_seeding_exploration
internal_flow.description: backend/exploration.py::execute_plan's create_card loop applies the identical treatment as step 6/7 to its own flashcard_review_state INSERT.
outputs: flashcard_review_state row seeded with scheduler metadata

internal_flow.name: migration_backfill_legacy_classic
internal_flow.description: One-time, sentinel-guarded UPDATE in schema.sql (folded from 10_schema.sql): every flashcard_review_state row with scheduler_assigned_at IS NULL AND last_reviewed_at IS NOT NULL -> scheduler='classic', scheduler_assigned_at=now(), scheduler_assignment_reason='legacy_retained_classic', experiment_version='sprint10_v1'. next_due_at/review_interval/last_reviewed_at are not in the SET list — untouched.
inputs: existing flashcard_review_state rows at first post-sprint startup

internal_flow.name: migration_backfill_never_reviewed
internal_flow.description: One-time, sentinel-guarded UPDATE in schema.sql: every flashcard_review_state row with scheduler_assigned_at IS NULL AND last_reviewed_at IS NULL -> scheduler = (hashtext(flashcard_id::text) % 2 = 0 ? 'classic' : 'fsrs'), scheduler_assigned_at=now(), scheduler_assignment_reason='migrated_never_reviewed_random', experiment_version='sprint10_v1'. Runs after step 9 in the same transaction so the two UPDATEs' WHERE clauses never overlap.
inputs: existing never-reviewed flashcard_review_state rows at first post-sprint startup
outputs: every previously-existing-but-unreviewed row permanently assigned via the balanced mechanism

internal_flow.name: due_row_scheduler_field

internal_flow.name: scheduler_badge_render
internal_flow.description: ReviewSessionView (src/ShellEntry.tsx) renders a small badge in the question card's top corner from queue[0].scheduler — 'Classic' or 'FSRS', visible before and after the answer is revealed, using existing Material 3 tokens. No new fetch — the value is already present on the same /due row the session already renders from.

internal_flow.name: experiment_summary_query
internal_flow.description: backend/routers/experiment.py::get_experiment_summary runs two aggregate queries — (a) GROUP BY scheduler over flashcard_review_state for assigned_cards/new_cards_assigned/migrated_cards_assigned/cards_new/cards_learning/cards_established (using the same review_interval='0'/<24h/>=24h thresholds CLAUDE.md already defines); (b) GROUP BY scheduler over review_events for reviewed_cards (count distinct flashcard_id)/completed_reviews (count *)/ordinary_due_reviews (count * filter prior_review_interval >= interval '24 hours')/failures (count * filter prior_review_interval >= interval '24 hours' and grade='again') — was_due is NOT used as the ordinary-due-review gate (see contracts.invariants); prior_review_interval >= 24h mirrors the app's existing learning/established threshold and correctly excludes rapid-retry/immediate-relearning reviews, which always follow a short (learning-phase) prior interval — then merges the two result sets in Python keyed by scheduler against a fixed ['classic','fsrs'] row list, coalescing every missing count to 0 and computing recall_rate = (ordinary_due_reviews - failures) / ordinary_due_reviews if ordinary_due_reviews > 0 else null.

deferred_decisions: Exact review_events retention/archival policy (unbounded append-only growth is accepted for this sprint; flagged as a Sprint 2 housekeeping follow-up)
Whether the experiment dashboard should eventually support per-essay/topic scoping (explicitly out of scope this sprint per non-goals; a natural Sprint 2 candidate)

risks.risk: FSRS-cohort cards will visibly reappear on a different rhythm (sub-hour learning-step intervals) than Classic cards during their first few reviews, since both flow through the identical RECENT/BACKLOG mechanism by design.
risks.impact: Expected and intentional per the mission ('the two algorithms will produce different due dates'), but early dashboard readings may look noisy until enough FSRS cards graduate past their learning steps — worth noting in the sprint report, not a defect.

risks.risk: fsrs_card_state.raw_state and its discrete sibling columns (stability/difficulty/fsrs_state/step/last_review_at) could drift if a future change writes one without the other.
risks.impact: Silent data-quality degradation in dashboard queries (which read the discrete columns) versus actual scheduling behavior (which reads raw_state) — mitigated by the invariant that both must always come from the same to_dict() call in the same statement.

risks.risk: The hash-based 50/50 split is only balanced in expectation, not exact, and is not stratified by essay/section/nugget/level.
risks.impact: Small cohorts (a newly-ingested essay) may show a visibly uneven local split even though the global split trends toward 50/50 — accepted per Phase B's explicit reasoning (a UUID-derived hash already balances any stratum in expectation); do not build a stratified sampler without a new design decision.

risks.risk: Review time is not reliably recorded anywhere in the current system (confirmed by Agent 1) and is therefore dropped from the dashboard scope entirely.
risks.impact: The dashboard cannot show a review-time/workload-per-minute comparison this sprint — documented as a known limitation, candidate for a Sprint 2 follow-up if review duration is ever captured.

open_questions.question: Should review_events eventually get a retention or summarization policy once it has accumulated many sprints of history?
Should the experiment dashboard eventually support per-essay/topic scoping, or remain system-wide only?
